quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted across traffic lanes?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes. They mark where drivers must stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass. It applies to both directions of traffic.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:

options.text: If you are on an expressway.

questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to your lane and a solid yellow line is next to the other lane, you may pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection is coming up. Watch carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
A driver may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after rain starts.
You need more space to stop.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous and slippery, especially when rain first starts. Water can cause your tires to lose grip. Slow down and leave extra space to stop.

questions.question: Alcohol-related crashes cause ____ of all motor vehicle deaths.
questions.explanation: Alcohol-related crashes cause 29 percent of all deaths from motor vehicle crashes. Driving while intoxicated is a serious problem.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or backward so they can see you.

questions.question: Which offense causes an automatic license suspension?

options.text: Failure to stop and help after a crash

questions.explanation: Your license is automatically suspended for certain offenses. These include driving while intoxicated, failing to stop and help after a crash, and driving with an invalid license.

questions.question: What is true about emergency vehicles?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Stop at regular intervals to rest.
Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at regular intervals to rest.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, take regular breaks. Rest and stretch your body, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, what should you know?

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
You must give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are in crosswalks.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are in crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. Crosswalks can be marked with horizontal lines, vertical lines, or both. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving near children playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run out in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and may run out in front of you without looking.

questions.question: You find a vehicle defect that affects safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe operation must be fixed as soon as possible. Fix defects before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign means traffic flows only in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: A vehicle is entering your freeway lane from an entrance ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.
Honk your horn so they know you are there.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.
Change lanes or slow down to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to make room.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. Change lanes when possible to let them merge safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down.

questions.question: When can you turn left with the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing left means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle using lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is ahead.

questions.question: How many seconds of following distance should you allow when driving behind a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep four to six seconds of distance between your car and a motorcycle. Even a small contact can cause the rider to fall or get hurt. This distance gives the rider time to stop or turn if needed.

questions.question: How close can you follow a fire truck that is using its siren?
questions.explanation: You must stay at least 500 feet away from a fire truck responding to a call. Do not drive or park your car in the same block where a fire truck has stopped.

questions.question: When can you safely pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because other cars are unlikely to be there.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
If you are next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass. All of these actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which types of medications can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Any medication can affect your driving ability. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about side effects before you drive. Check the labels on over-the-counter medicines to see if they can impair your driving.

questions.question: What is the legal blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit for drivers age 21 and older?
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It makes you feel overly confident.
It reduces your ability to think clearly.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and affects your balance. Alcohol also impairs your vision and your ability to judge distance, making it harder to respond to what is around you.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal to slow down on a slippery road. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: What must you do if a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Follow what other cars are doing instead of the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of a crossing guard in a school zone. Slow down and be extra careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-lane, two-way road?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your car has enough speed to pass.

questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-lane, two-way road if you can see far ahead, you can get back to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your car can reach the speed needed to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.
